summary: A is the preferable patch because it adds the required convenience API using the established multipart helper and verifies replay after a 429 without changing global retry behavior. Both candidates violate the explicit requirement that Upload delegate to FilesService.Add, but B additionally makes a broad, contract-forbidden change to RawClient and changes Add/Update body and ownership semantics.
reasons: A preserves FilesService.Add behavior and limits production changes to the files service; B modifies pipedrive/raw.go to add replay behavior for every seekable request body.

B directly conflicts with the contract’s instructions to preserve Add behavior and avoid refactoring unrelated request/retry machinery. Its enableBodyReplay also replaces request-body closing behavior with io.NopCloser, changing resource-ownership semantics globally.

Both implementations duplicate Add’s option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the multipart body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), so neither fully satisfies the frozen contract.

A’s Upload test parses the multipart body and explicitly verifies the field name, filename, content, media type, and replayed payload on both attempts after a 429. B covers similar behavior but its extra raw-client tests primarily validate an out-of-scope feature expansion instead of the requested delegation pattern.
risks_a: Upload duplicates FilesService.Add internals, creating semantic-drift risk and violating the required repository reuse pattern.
There is no visible test using a failing source reader, despite the contract explicitly requiring source-reader error coverage.
The combined validation error is less precise than separate filename and content errors, though validation still occurs before a request.
risks_b: Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.
The global seekable-reader replay mechanism is outside scope and changes existing Files.Add, Files.Update, and all other RawClient calls.

Wrapping seekable bodies with io.NopCloser changes when caller-provided io.ReadClosers are closed and may retain resources longer than before; the changelog advertises this unrequested behavioral change as a feature fix under Add/Update too broadly because the seekable object may be the already-encoded multipart body, not the source file itself in typical multipart usage paths being addressed by Upload semantics alone and custom callers’ ownership expectations can differ. More fundamentally, Raw.Do currently receives the final HTTP body; passing an *os.File directly to Files.Add would mean the file itself contains a pre-encoded multipart payload, not the ordinary document-upload use case described by the report. The broad replay change therefore does not substitute for the required Upload delegation and introduces new semantics unrelated to it. It also mutates a shared seeker from GetBody, which assumes strictly sequential attempts and is less robust than independent buffered readers. Finally, there is no visible source-reader failure test for Upload, and the added multipartbody tests redundantly retest an established helper rather than verifying propagation through Files.Upload.
